U: › [ U ] how quickly you do something
› [ U ] how easy or difficult something is
› [ U ] UK the condition of the ground for walking or riding, etc.

S: › [ S ] an occasion when someone leaves somewhere

NONE: › UK available or existing
可得到的；現有的；現行的
› used to refer to the activity of going to the stated place
去（某個場所）的；參加（某活動）的
› the usual rate, price, etc. at a particular time
（在某特定時期）通常的比率/價格/工資（等等）

example: The traffic was terrible so it was slow going.
交通狀況很糟糕，所以進展很慢。
She's obviously very intelligent, but her lectures are heavy going (= they are difficult to understand).
顯然她很有才智，但是她的課太難懂了。
At first the job was hard going (= difficult), but it's got easier with time.
一開始的時候，這項工作很難，可是隨著時間的推移，現在容易一些了。
After an inch of rain at the racecourse overnight, the going is described as good to soft.
由於第一天晚上的降雨量達到了一英寸，據說賽馬場的場地稍偏軟。
His going came as a shock.
他的離去令大家都很震驚。
I wouldn't trust him if I were you - he's the biggest crook going (= he's the most dishonest person that exists).
如果我是你就不會相信他——他是當今世上最大的騙子。
I don't suppose there's any left-over pie going, is there?
我想派餅一點也沒有剩下吧，是不是？
£30 an hour is the going rate for a piano teacher.
鋼琴老師通常的收費是一小時30英鎊。
He grew up in a strict church-going family.
他在一個恪守教規、定期去教堂做禮拜的家庭中長大。

NONE: › In sports, if a team or person wins a competition going away, they win it by a lot of points, goals, etc.
（體育比賽中）大獲全勝

example: They seemed to score at will in the final period and the Knicks won going away.
在比賽最後階段，他們打得十分順利，彷彿得分是隨心所欲的事，最終尼克隊大獲全勝。

NONE: › UK also going on for informal nearly or almost (a particular number, age, time, or amount)
接近（某個數目、年齡、時間或數量）
› humorous used for saying that someone behaves like a much older person
實際上…歲，行為舉止卻像…歲

example: It was going on midnight when we left the party.
我們離開聚會時都快午夜了。
There were going on 200 people at their wedding.
有近200人參加他們的婚禮。

NONE: › a sale of goods at reduced prices by a shop that is going to stop doing business and close
歇業大拍賣
› an activity such as cleaning that is done carefully and completely
徹底做的事情；仔仔細細做的事情
› UK informal an occasion when someone is hit repeatedly
被毒打，被痛打

example: This carpet's filthy! It needs a really good going-over.
這地毯太骯髒了！要好好洗一洗。
Detectives have given the apartment a thorough going-over (= examined it carefully).
偵探們把公寓仔細搜查了一次。
They said I'd get a real going-over if I didn't pay them by tomorrow.
他們說如果我明天還不給他們錢，他們就會狠狠打我一頓。

NONE: › strange, unusual, humorous, or unsuitable events or activities
（怪異、罕見、可笑或不當的）事情，活動，勾當

example: There've been a lot of strange/odd goings-on in that house recently.
最近那座房子裡發生了很多莫名其妙的事情。

NONE: › a swelling at the front of the neck caused by an increase in size of the thyroid gland
甲狀腺腫
